name: How much contingency should I keep for a custom home in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What contingency percentage is normal for a custom home build in LA?
mainEntity.text: What contingency percentage is normal for a custom home build in LA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Contingency is one of the most overlooked parts of a custom home budget. In Los Angeles, the right reserve depends on how much is known about the lot and how detailed the design is. A flatter site with a well-defined plan may need less contingency than a hillside lot or a project with uncertain soil, access, or design changes. Homeowners should think of contingency as protection against surprises, not as extra spending money. The best practice is to set it aside early and avoid using it for optional upgrades unless the base budget is secure. Builders who do not include contingency in early discussions often make the project look cheaper than it really is.
acceptedAnswer.description: A common contingency for custom home building is about 10% to 20% of the project budget, with higher reserves needed for hillside lots, remodel-plus-addition projects, or highly customized luxury homes. The more unknowns in the site and design, the larger the contingency should be.
